title: Workload Episodic Profiling + Safe Apply Runbook for Continuous Batching Advisor
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build an episodic workload profiler and an operator-facing runbook to safely recommend and apply continuous batching parameters (min_batch_size, max_wait_ms, kv_prefetch_ratio) with automatic rollback triggers. Scope: 1) lightweight profiler that segments workloads into 'episodes' (burst, steady, quiet) using request inter-arrival and token distribution; 2) heuristic engine that synthesizes cohort-level recommendations combining cost-slope, p99 latency delta, and cache hit sensitivity; 3) safe-apply mechanism: shadow apply -> canary cohort -> staged rollout with automatic rollback rules; 4) operator runbook and dashboards for post-apply troubleshooting. Acceptance criteria: - Profiler produces episode labels with >85% agreement on hand-labeled traces across 3 representative customers. - Recommendations reduce per-token cost by >=6% on synthetic mixed workloads without p99 latency regressions >10%. - Safe-apply completes staged rollout and triggers automated rollback on defined safety signals in integration tests. Key heuristics: - Episode detection: sliding window inter-arrival entropy + short-tail token distribution change. Episodes classify as BURST / STEADY / QUIET. - Recommendation scoring: score = w_cost * expected_token_cost_reduction - w_lat * expected_p99_increase - w_risk * cache_sensitivity_penalty. Default weights tuned from 1000+ collected traces. - KV-awareness: if cache hit ratio expected < 40% for an episode, favor lower max_wait_ms and smaller min_batch_size; if hit ratio > 70% allow larger max_wait_ms and higher coalescence. - Throttling & safety knobs: max rollout velocity (percent nodes/min), canary size (default 2%), shadow-apply sampling (5% traffic mirrored), revert window (15 minutes). Rollback triggers (automatic): - p99 latency increases >15% sustained for 3 minutes AND error rate increase >0.3% OR - token cost increases >8% for 10 minutes OR - tail-critical errors (model OOM / 5xx) recorded on canary. Observability: - Add telemetry tags: episode_type, cohort_id, applied_config_hash, pre_apply_metrics (p50/p95/p99, cpu_gpu_util, cost_per_token). - Dashboards: per-cohort latency/cost curve, episode heatmap, rollout timeline. Implementation plan (high level): 1) Profiler service (lightweight) embedded in request router to emit episode tags and summary windows; 2) Offline scoring and simulation pipeline to run recommendations against historical windows; 3) Safe-apply controller integrated with rollout service: shadow -> canary -> staged; 4) Runbook + incident playbook and alerting. Trade-offs & decisions: - On-path profiling provides more accurate episodes but increases router CPU; we opted for sample-based on-path with low-overhead C aggregator (default sample 1/1000). - Conservative defaults prioritized for customer safety; aggressive tuning moved to opt-in experimental flag. - We will not modify model code; changes limited to routing and batching layer to reduce blast radius. Artifacts: design doc (Confluence), simulation notebooks, integration test harness, and operator runbook.
